question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the sponsor and manager of the AIF shall act in what capacity towards its investors?

answer.text: Principal-to-principal capacity with no ongoing duty after investment
Fiduciary capacity, with an obligation to disclose all conflicts as and when they arise or seem likely to arise
Arms-length capacity consistent with a commercial counterparty
Trustee-only capacity limited to safekeeping of assets

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7 (Regulation on Governance Structure in AIF), the SEBI (AIF) Regulations expressly state the sponsor and manager shall act in a fiduciary capacity toward investors and disclose all conflicts as and when they arise or seem likely to arise. This creates an ongoing duty of care and loyalty. The Trap: Principal-to-principal and arms-length framings wrongly eliminate ongoing fiduciary duty. Trustee-only is too narrow — the trustee role is separate from the manager's fiduciary role. Cross-Exam Context: Fiduciary-capacity language is common across XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C, XXI-A, XXI-B and X-A/X-B. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the Investment Management Agreement, explicitly restate the fiduciary standard — some trustees take a narrow 'administrative' view and the IMA must pre-empt that by affirming the Manager's ongoing fiduciary role.
